title: Carrier oils, butters and waxes - data table

how_to_read.saponification: naoh/koh = grams of lye per gram of oil (soapmaker SAP). mg KOH/g (lab SV) / 1000 = koh; koh x 40.00/56.11 = naoh.
how_to_read.iodine_value: g I2 absorbed per 100 g (Wijs). Higher = more double bonds = softer, faster rancidity, and (above ~130-140) drying-oil behaviour.
how_to_read.fatty_acids: percent of total fatty acids. Soapee/SoapCalc rows often do not sum to 100 and omit minor or unusual acids - several are corrected below with literature ranges.
how_to_read.codex_ranges: where Codex covers an oil these ranges are authoritative for food-grade identity and override the soaper table.

comedogenic_caveat: Comedogenic numbers come from the rabbit-ear assay (Kligman/Fulton era, e.g. Fulton 1989 J Soc Cosmet Chem 40:321-333; Fulton 1984 J Am Acad Dermatol PMID 6229554). The rabbit ear over-predicts human comedogenicity, tested many materials neat or at 10% in propylene glycol, and popular 0-5 lists online frequently cite no source at all. Treat as a weak hint; a finished formula must be judged on its own.
smoke_point_caveat: Smoke point is method-dependent and falls with free fatty acids, age and reuse; figures are commonly cited ranges, not primary-verified.

oils.name: Olive oil (extra virgin / virgin / refined / pomace)

codex_ranges.source: Codex Alimentarius CXS 33-1981 (rev. 2015) Standard for olive oils and olive pomace oils

ins_value.source: Soapee/SoapCalc (INS = SAP(KOH mg/g) - iodine; a soaper heuristic, not a lab standard)

melting_point_c.note: refrigeration clouding is wax/saturate crystallisation, not a purity test

oxidative_stability.shelf_life: 18-24 months from harvest for EVOO, cool and dark
oxidative_stability.native_antioxidants: hydroxytyrosol, oleuropein-aglycone secoiridoids, tocopherols (EVOO only; refining strips polyphenols)

comedogenic.basis: attributed to Fulton 1989 (original table not re-checked)

skin_feel_absorption.skin_note: Danby 2013 (PMID 22995032): neat olive oil on adult forearms for 4 weeks damaged the stratum corneum barrier and raised TEWL, sunflower oil did not; caution on neonatal/atopic skin.

smoke_point_c.note: Smoke point is method-dependent and falls with free fatty acids, age and reuse; figures are commonly cited ranges, not primary-verified. EVOO is oxidatively robust in frying studies despite its modest smoke point because of MUFA plus polyphenols.

oils.culinary: All-purpose; EVOO for dressings, finishing, saute and moderate frying; refined/pomace for high heat.
oils.refined_vs_unrefined: EVOO: mechanical only, below 27 C malaxation for "cold extraction" (EU Reg. 29/2012). Refined/pomace: deodorised, polyphenol-poor, neutral.
oils.allergen: Rare (olive pollen allergy is common, olive-oil food allergy is very rare).
oils.notes: Pure-olive (castile) soap is slow to trace, soft at first and needs 6+ months cure; its lather is low and slimy-feeling.
oils.verification: Codex ranges verified from CXS 33 PDF; SAP verified vs SoapCalc; Danby PMID verified via PubMed E-utilities.

oils.name: Coconut oil, virgin (and refined "76 degree")

codex_ranges.source: Codex Alimentarius CXS 210-1999 (rev. 2015), Table 1 and Appendix (GLC ranges, % of total fatty acids; SV mg KOH/g; IV Wijs)

ins_value.source: Soapee/SoapCalc (INS = SAP(KOH mg/g) - iodine; a soaper heuristic, not a lab standard)

oxidative_stability.rating: excellent (saturated) but prone to hydrolytic/soapy rancidity if wet

comedogenic.basis: attributed to Fulton 1989 (original table not re-checked)

skin_feel_absorption.feel: melts on contact, then slick; can feel drying in soap

smoke_point_c.note: Smoke point is method-dependent and falls with free fatty acids, age and reuse; figures are commonly cited ranges, not primary-verified.

oils.culinary: Baking, curries, frying (refined). Highest saturated-fat cooking oil (~90% saturated).
oils.refined_vs_unrefined: Virgin (fresh meat, coconut aroma) vs RBD (copra, refined-bleached-deodorised, neutral). "76 degree" refers to melt point in F.
oils.allergen: FDA historically listed coconut as a tree nut for labelling; botanically a drupe/palm seed; true coconut allergy is uncommon. (FDA tree-nut list was narrowed in its 2025 allergen guidance - status not re-verified here.)
best_uses: soap (cleansing/lather; usually <=30% at 5%+ superfat, or 100% at ~20% superfat)

oils.name: Coconut oil, fractionated / MCT

fatty_acids.note: Caprylic C8:0 50-65 + capric C10:0 30-45 (MCT oil spec); lauric removed. Soapee lists 54/43.

ins_value.source: Soapee/SoapCalc (INS = SAP(KOH mg/g) - iodine; a soaper heuristic, not a lab standard)

smoke_point_c.refined: ~160 (MCT burns/smokes low; not a frying oil)
smoke_point_c.note: Smoke point is method-dependent and falls with free fatty acids, age and reuse; figures are commonly cited ranges, not primary-verified.

oils.culinary: Food MCT oil in drinks; not for frying.
oils.notes: Do NOT use in soap calculations as ordinary coconut - SAP 0.232 NaOH, and it does not make a bar. Highly stable carrier for dosed oils.

oils.name: Jojoba oil (a liquid wax ester, not a triglyceride)

fatty_acids.source: literature range, compiled from general lipid references (Gunstone, The Lipid Handbook; Firestone, Physical and Chemical Characteristics of Oils, Fats and Waxes) - not re-checked line by line this session
fatty_acids.note: ~97% straight-chain wax esters (C38-C44). Only ~50% saponifiable -> SAP is low; it stays as unsaponifiable "superfat" in soap.

oxidative_stability.rating: excellent - among the most oxidation-stable carriers

skin_feel_absorption.feel: dry, satiny, resembles human sebum wax esters

oils.culinary: Not a food oil: largely indigestible wax esters, laxative; not GRAS as a food oil.
oils.verification: SAP verified (0.066 NaOH SoapCalc); composition from literature, unverified this session.

oils.name: Castor oil

fatty_acids.note: Ricinoleic acid (12-hydroxy-oleic) 85-95%. Viscous, humectant-like, solvent for resins and pigments.

ins_value.source: Soapee/SoapCalc (INS = SAP(KOH mg/g) - iodine; a soaper heuristic, not a lab standard)

oils.culinary: Not a cooking oil; stimulant laxative (ricinoleic acid acts on EP3 prostanoid receptors - Tunaru 2012 PNAS, not re-verified).
oils.refined_vs_unrefined: Cold-pressed (the oil is free of ricin; ricin stays in the meal/cake, which is why heat-treated cake is a safety step).
oils.allergen: Castor-bean (meal) allergy is occupational; the oil itself rarely.
oils.notes: In soap above ~10-15% it makes a soft, sticky bar.

codex_ranges.source: Codex Alimentarius CXS 210-1999 (rev. 2015), Table 1 and Appendix (GLC ranges, % of total fatty acids; SV mg KOH/g; IV Wijs)

oils.culinary: Deep frying, wok; long-chain saturates (behenic/lignoceric) make it cloud in the fridge.
oils.allergen: PEANUT - THE REFINING QUESTION: Hourihane et al. 1997 BMJ (PMID 9133891), double-blind challenge of 60 peanut-allergic people: refined peanut oil caused no reactions; crude (cold-pressed) oil caused reactions in 6 of 60 (10%). Highly refined oils are exempt from US major-allergen labelling under FALCPA 2004 (and EU Annex II for refined soy oil; EU does NOT exempt peanut oil generally). Gourmet/roasted/expeller oils, and refined oil that has been used to fry other foods, are not safe assumptions. Topical: Lack 2003 NEJM (PMID 12637607) associated peanut-oil-containing skin preparations in infancy with later peanut allergy - avoid peanut oil in baby balms/lotions.
oils.verification: Codex verified; SAP verified; both PMIDs verified via PubMed E-utilities.

oils.culinary: Bengali, Punjabi, Kashmiri, Bihari cooking, pickles (achar); infant/adult massage oil in South Asia.
oils.allergen: MUSTARD is an EU major allergen (Annex II, Reg. 1169/2011).
oils.notes: Erucic acid: myocardial lipidosis in rats drove the move to LEAR canola. US FDA does not permit expressed mustard oil to be sold as a food oil (import alert; sold labelled "for external use only") - not re-verified. EFSA 2016 TDI 7 mg/kg bw/day. Argemone-oil adulteration of mustard oil caused epidemic dropsy outbreaks in India (Delhi 1998) - buy from trusted sources.
oils.verification: Codex verified; SAP verified (0.123 NaOH); regulatory notes unverified this session.
